leads.summary: #10215 extracts the unfixed calendar hero into CalendarView.qml

leads.summary: Three localization PRs make the unchanged hero-date assertion fail after a clean Panel merge
leads.consequence: #9155 changes the date expression to toLocaleDateString, #7173 to Qt.locale().toString, and #7434 to labelLocale.toString. Each produces a conflict-free merged Panel with this PR's width code, but the kept clock test requires the literal Qt.formatDate(root.today, "MMMM d") and exits 1 before its four new layout assertions. #7173 and #7434 also edit that test, so their test merges have conflicts. When integrating any of these, assert the actual locale-aware date expression instead of reinstating the old formatter.
leads.triage: factual but pre-existing: clock-test.sh:215 assertion is not introduced or changed by this PR; dropped

leads.summary: Two competing hero-scaling PRs conflict with the new font bindings
leads.consequence: #13459 and #13463 both replace the original 48/52px with fontScale formulas where this PR replaces them with Style.space(). Neither is stacked; each creates two unresolved merge-file conflicts in Panel.qml. #13459 additionally conflicts in the clock test and expects a fontScale formula incompatible with the new Style.space(52) assertion. Select one scale (taking [spacing] overrides into account), reconcile the test, and do not merge both independently.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (#13459/#13463 fontScale conflict); corroboration

leads.summary: Hero typography follows the spacing override instead of font base-size
leads.consequence: With supported [spacing] scale-with-font=false, lowering [font] base-size from 12 to 10 leaves Style.space(48/52) at 48/52px, although the rest of the type scale shrinks to base 10. Conversely changing [spacing] scale alone changes the date's font size. The promised date/icon shrink on a small-text setup is absent under this supported override; a screen-capped narrow popup still has to fit or elide the original 52px date. For hero typography meant to follow the font preference, multiply 48/52 by Style.fontScale rather than Style.space, and keep margins/widths on Style.space.
leads.triage: factual; verified Style.qml:207-222 and docs/omarchy-shell.md:262-273; no clipping risk because popup width uses the same function; published as comment-accuracy note

leads.summary: #11639's hero-sized content introduces feedback into the new date-width binding
leads.consequence: The clean merged source uses heroRow.implicitWidth to set both panel contentWidth and calendarColumn.width; this PR sets heroDate.width from heroBox.width, which follows calendarColumn.width. This is a circular geometry dependency when the hero is wider than the grid. The merged static tests pass, so they do not settle whether Qt stabilizes it, warns about a binding loop, or initially collapses the date. Reproduce with the combined QML on a narrow layout or ask the full reviewer to confirm the rendered dimensions before posting it as a runtime defect.
leads.triage: hypothesis contradicted by Opus combo runs (49/49 identical to head, no binding loops); dropped

leads.summary: The four new layout assertions accept a date that still overhangs the row
leads.consequence: A plausible one-token edit to the changed expression, using + heroRow.spacing instead of - heroRow.spacing, makes a constrained date plus icon plus gap exceed heroBox by twice the gap and clips the end again. All four new assertions still pass because they only recognize the earlier heroBox.width - heroIcon.implicitWidth substring, the row expression, and token presence. Positive original and negative removing the row width establish the fixture executes and can fail. Assert the full budget expression and preferably actual narrow-width geometry.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus test note; confirmed by reading the regex; published (spacing term not covered)

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change stops the calendar hero from clipping whenever the popup is at least as wide as the calendar grid; on narrower screens the hero now scrolls with the grid instead of losing its left edge. At the default text size, the hero is unchanged wherever it already fitted. Results from an offscreen Qt 6.11.2 replica of the popup width chain, with the default JetBrainsMono Nerd Font and "September 30":

| Case | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Text size 9 (viewport 394 px) | Row 427 px, clipped 17 px left and 16 px right | Date at 39 px, row 324 px, fits |
| Screen-capped popup (viewport 428 px) | Clipped 2 px on each side | Date at 51 px, fits exactly |
| Text size 12 (default), wherever the base hero fits | Fits | Identical geometry in all 35 comparable cases |

- No binding-loop warnings in 307 layout cases (a deliberate loop used as a control was detected).
- The icon stays baseline-aligned with the date in every case.
- `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` passes 159/159 at the head, and also with the head applied to the current `quattro` tip. `qml-text-format-test.sh` passes 19/19.

The reported clipping at base-size 10 did not reproduce with the default font and theme (the base row fits with 6 px to spare on the left and about 5 px on the right). A different font or theme border could explain the report; the device itself was not tested.

### Hero size now changes at every non-default text size

Most of the fix comes from the second commit, which replaces the fixed 48/52 px icon and date with `Style.space(48)` / `Style.space(52)`. `Text.HorizontalFit` rarely engages at real popup widths with the default font; it acts as a safety net. The scaling applies to everyone, not only narrow panels:

| Text size | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 14 | 16 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Date px | 39 | 43 | 48 | 52 | 61 | 69 | 87 |
| Icon px | 36 | 40 | 44 | 48 | 56 | 64 | 80 |

**Impact:** the hero visibly shrinks at text sizes below 12 and grows above it (at 20, "September 30" is 626 px wide instead of 374 px). The PR description's Fix section does not mention this; only the commit message does. The weather panel hero stays fixed at 64/56 px (`shell/plugins/panels/weather/Panel.qml`), so the two heroes will differ at non-default sizes.

**Suggested change:** mention the scaling in the PR description, so the visible change is reviewed as intended behavior.

### Overlapping open PRs and unlinked issues

| PR | Relationship to this PR |
|---|---|
| #11639 | Alternative fix: widens the popup to the hero instead of shrinking the hero. Merges without textual conflict, but combined, its widening has no effect (the replica matched this head in all 49 combined cases). |
| #13459, #13463 | Both "Fixes #13381". Scale the same two font lines with `Math.max(1, Math.round(N * Style.fontScale))` and conflict with this PR in `Panel.qml`. `Style.fontScale` ignores `[spacing] scale`, which the popup width follows; `Style.space` here follows the same scale as the popup width. |
| #10215 | Moves the calendar hero into a new `CalendarView.qml` that keeps fixed `font.pixelSize: 48` / `52` with no width budget, and conflicts with this PR. If it lands, this fix would need porting there. |

Issues #11629 and #13381 describe this bug and are not linked from the PR.

**Impact:** several fixes for the same clipping are open at once. #13459 and #13463 conflict with this PR, and if #11639 is merged alongside it, #11639's widening silently has no effect.

**Suggested change:** link #11629 and #13381, and note the relationship to #11639, #13459 and #13463 so one approach can be chosen.

**Optional test improvement:** three of the new assertions match `/id: heroDate[\s\S]*?.../`, which is not bounded to the `heroDate` element (the first uses the same unbounded pattern from `id: heroBox`). Moving `fontSizeMode: Text.HorizontalFit` and `minimumPixelSize: 28` from `heroDate` to the later `monthLabel` Text still passes 159/159, and the width assertion does not cover the `- heroRow.spacing` term. The first assertion checks the `heroRow` width clamp, which only takes effect when the container is narrower than the icon plus spacing (about 58 px at the default text size). Slicing the `heroDate` block before matching, and matching the whole width expression, would make these assertions fail when the properties move or the budget changes.

**Comment and description notes:**
- The new comment in `Panel.qml` (lines 296-305) still says "the date is a fixed 52px", which the second commit changed.
- The same comment cites "a notch-anchored 500px variant"; no such variant appears elsewhere in the repository.
- The font comments say the size follows "the text-size scale". `Style.space` follows `[spacing] scale` as well, and with `scale-with-font = false` it does not follow text size at all.
- The PR description says two regression assertions were added; the diff adds four.
- The repository's `AGENTS.md` asks for visual changes to be verified in the running UI. A before/after screenshot at the reported setting would support the device report.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `e7012db` against the base and the current `quattro` tip, plus Qt 6.11.2 `qquicktext.cpp` and `qquickpositioners.cpp`. Isolated offscreen QML runs of the verbatim hero block in a replica of the popup width chain, with stubbed `Style`, `Color` and tooltip (not the live shell), installed fonts only and default theme borders. Repository test runs, including diagnostic mutants. Textual merge checks against the open PRs listed above. No running-desktop or device test.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
